description.en: A source-verified MiniMax H3 action prompt with attached video evidence from @ou_zhen599.
description.zh: 由原作者公开 X 帖提供并已核验视频结果的 MiniMax H3动作提示词。

prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, realistic cyberpunk thriller. The first frame fully matches <Picture 1>. Preserve exact continuity throughout: Subject A is the driver with black hair, a cold restrained expression, a mechanical prosthetic arm, and the same white heavy motorcycle; Subject B is the rear passenger with red hair, a pale trench coat, wet hair clinging to the skin, and an initially fragile but later dangerous presence. Keep the same faces, hair colors, body proportions, age impression, costumes, prosthetic details, and motorcycle design from <Picture 1>. No new characters, no costume or hairstyle drift, no face drift, no body drift, no subtitles, no watermark. The entire story stays inside the same narrow rain-soaked cyberpunk alley near the reflective wet wall at the alley end. The ground is slick, the walls are damp, neon signs cast mixed red and blue reflections, the air holds cold mist, and the space feels compressed. The camera is intimate and functional, using a few dense close and medium-close shots; the first half flows, the second half steadies. A always remains in front controlling the motorcycle with a low forward lean. B always remains pressed close behind, first dependent, then silently dangerous. [Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the camera cuts from an ultra-low tracking view near the front wheel tearing through rainwater, rises into A’s half-profile, then drifts to the rear-view mirror where B’s eyes appear. B breathes slightly fast, glances toward the pressure behind them, then toward A, and quietly says: <d>[English] They’re close.</d> A stays controlled and forward-facing. [Shot 3] At 00:05.500, the shot cuts to a diagonal rear medium-close tracking angle as the motorcycle leans low and skims past the wet wall. Red and blue neon sweep across both faces. B presses closer and grips A’s waist side, implying dependence. A does not turn back, only checks B once through the rear-view mirror, then says in a low compressed tone: <d>[English] Hold on. Don’t look around.</d> The line feels protective and commanding. [Shot 4] At 00:08.500, the shot cuts tighter on both upper bodies, then pushes into an extreme close-up of B’s hand. Still pressed close, B silently draws a thin blade or micro-injector from inside the trench coat and brings it to the side of A’s neck. The move is small, efficient, and nearly hidden by their intimacy. B’s eyes lock cold, her mouth line flattens, her breathing stabilizes, and the false helplessness disappears. She says quietly and precisely: <d>[English] You didn’t come to save me.</d> [Shot 5] At 00:11.500, the camera alternates between an extreme close-up of A’s eye and the rear-view mirror. A remains unnervingly steady, then gives a short controlled brake tap. The motorcycle decelerates just enough on the wet road to throw B’s body forward by half an inch and spoil the weapon angle. At the same instant, A’s left shoulder drives subtly backward to steal space. The action stays fully physical and believable through brake pressure, slick-road resistance, inertia, and the tiny forward jolt. A calmly replies: <d>[English] And you didn’t come to leave with me.</d> [Shot 6] At 00:13.000, the motorcycle performs a precise sliding stop at the alley end in front of the reflective wet wall. The camera moves to a front-side 45-degree angle and settles into a composition where both characters appear together in the reflective wall surface. The geometry locks them in the same frame. A’s hidden countermeasure device is already raised in the other hand, aimed at B through the reflected composition. A lifts the gaze toward B’s reflection rather than turning into a dramatic pose and says in a low voice: <d>[English] The moment you got on, I was waiting for this.</d> B does not explode emotionally; she only shows a brief stall and tightened pupils. Hold on the reflected standoff through the end, with no fade to black and no cut away. Keep the acting restrained and realistic: A stays cold, minimal, and highly controlling, with eyes moving before speech and very little mouth or jaw change; B begins with quick breath, wet-hair vulnerability, and help-seeking closeness, then becomes cold and controlled after the weapon reveal. Lighting stays cold and wet with red-blue neon sweeps, motorcycle headlight shaping the bodies, realistic wet skin, subtle prosthetic highlights, visible road oil and damp wall texture, and preserved detail in the dark areas. Maintain spatial and physical coherence in the same alley from start to finish with no teleporting, no wide fight, no extra vehicles intruding, no exaggerated stunts, no cartoon expression, no face collapse, no oversized mouth shapes, no limb deformation, and no overacting.

overall_soundscape: Heavy realistic rain runs through the full 15 seconds with tire spray, wet-road hiss, subtle electric motor presence, close urban electrical buzz, and damp-wall reflections. Dialogue stays tightly synced to restrained mouth movement and breath rhythm. Add wet fabric friction, the faint blade or injector reveal, a short brake tap, slick-pavement tire friction, the tiny forward body jolt, the controlled sliding stop, scattered water, and a subtle readiness sound from A’s hidden countermeasure.

non_diegetic_music: A low-frequency suspended electronic thriller score with minimal melody. Keep it understated under the rain and vehicle motion, tighten it after B’s weapon reveal with colder pulses, add a brief tension accent at the brake-tap reversal, and thin it slightly in the final reflective standoff while preserving unresolved pressure.
